notes: The release chain's stages in order, read by scripts/ci/release-watch.ts (cloud #264). Each stage runs from its own start (from) to its own end (to), so stages can overlap: since cloud #471 the staging copy (staging_publish) and the staging deploy both start when hosted_release ends. A stage that has not started yet counts from what it waits on (after), so a stall still shows; tag, pin_open, pin_merge, direct_pin and redline_queue are the hand-off waits between events. from as a list is the latest of those events (redline_queue starts when both the copy and the deploy have ended). A stage is done only once its own run or job completed green: the staging and prod copies end when their publish-staging or publish-prod job does, though the run goes on.

Events: merged (the oldest public PR merged into the release), published (the public release), pin_opened (the pin-bump/<tag> PR opened), pinned (the pin commit on cloud main: the PR's merge, or the direct pin commit), then <step>.started and <step>.done for the runs (or jobs) of hosted_release, staging_publish, staging_deploy, redline, prod_publish and prod_deploy, and fleet from the prod deploy's steps. Once the prod deploy's Wake the fleet step has started, the deploy's own work is done there, so prod_deploy ends at that step's start.
mode pr stages count only for a release pinned through a pin-bump PR, mode direct only for one pinned by a direct commit on main. pinMode is the mode a release with neither yet is waiting in.

usual is each stage's median in minutes over every measured release below where that stage finished green (a red stage is not counted). They are the 23 public releases v0.235.2 to v0.248.2, read by a read-only backfill tick (release-watch.ts tick --since 2026-11-20 --no-issue) at 2026-11-26T06:55Z, each stage timed from its own start. n per stage: tag 23, pin_open 18, pin_merge 16, hosted_release 14, staging_publish 16, staging_deploy 16, redline_queue 16, redline 11, prod_publish 11, prod_deploy 11.

direct_pin has no measured release yet: its usual 2.15 is an estimate, pin_open's median, since the same pin-bump run makes the pin commit instead of opening the PR. Measure it once releases pin directly.

The alert: one comment per release and stage, on the one open issue titled release stuck, when any stage of any release a run sees (in flight, done, superseded or in history; each judged on its own runs) finished past its limit, or a stage of a release not done failed; a stage of a release in flight seen still running past its limit gets its own still running comment, once. The watcher runs on events only (no schedule, no poll), so a stage that goes past its limit with no event after it is the release agent's to catch. The limit is max(alertFactor x usual, usual + alertFloor) minutes, so max(2 x usual, usual + 5 min): the floor keeps a stage that usually takes half a minute (redline_queue) from alerting on a one-minute wait. e2eTarget is merge to every install in minutes: every release's total is reported against it in the summary, never alerted on. A release whose prod deploy records no fleet finish has its total to the prod deploy, and the summary says so: to prod deploy (fleet not yet measured).

A run belongs to a release by its verified identity, never by the sha it ran on alone: hosted-release by its hosted-built <tag> <sha> job (cloud #469) or else the pin commit it ran on; the staging publish by its publish-staging release <tag> job, so a recovery run on a later main commit counts (v0.246.1: run 45730519720 on fd2652f3); the rest by their run names. A release that reached its prod deploy is never superseded.

fleet runs from the prod deploy's successful Wake the fleet step's start to the fleet's finish; a wake that failed or was cancelled fails prod_deploy (cloud #495), with a failed-stage comment, unless another run of the tag woke the fleet; one skipped on purpose (an older tag, a partial target list) anchors nothing and raises nothing on its own. Since cloud #495 the deploy does not wait for the fleet: the finish comes from a later prod deploy, which reads every fleet_done mark the platform holds and runs a successful step named Fleet done of earlier releases (<tag> at <ISO time>, <tag> at <ISO time>, ...), oldest first, the newest 20 at most. Each listed time is that tag's exact finish, the scheduler's own fleet_done time; the earliest per tag across every run wins, and a release already in history takes it too. Until the next prod deploy records it, the fleet is pending and the release's total is to prod deploy (fleet not yet measured). Runs from before #495 also have a Wait for the fleet to reach every install step and a Fleet done step that ran once every install was upgraded, within a 10 min wait; that step's end is an upper bound some seconds after the mark, labelled as such until a record corrects it. The steps are read from the runs' jobs with the default token. fleet has no usual time yet, so it never alerts. The watcher never reads fleet state through admin tools.
